newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei ends lower on more corporate woes.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei ends lower on more corporate woes.

text.p: Weak technicals, coupled with continued corporate woes in Japan, pressured SIMEX 225-share Nikkei index futures lower on Friday, dealers said.
"There was a sell-out in Nikkei, especially after a sell-off in the construction sector in Tokyo following the Tokai Kogyo news," said a dealer with a local institution.
Japanese construction firm Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd, with a debt of 510 billion yen, was said to have applied for court protection under bankruptcy laws earlier on Friday.

"There is just one bad news after another from Japan. In Singapore, people are very cautious just in case there is another brewing which Tokyo is more or less aware (of) and we are not," said another dealer.
The benchmark September Nikkei futures ended 250 points down at 19,930 after several sell-stops were triggered. Volume was about 11,748 lots.
Dealers said a shift of investors' interest towards more lucrative bonds also dampened the Nikkei.

"The Nikkei looks weak but we should not think the market is on a definite down path because it has discounted quite a lot recently. Any climb above 20,000 will be helpful," said the dealer with the local institution.
He pegged its next support at 19,750.
Dealers said they awaited fresh developments from the Tokai press conference scheduled for 0900 GMT on Friday.
The SIMEX Taiwan stock futures index ended at 391.2 against 384.7 previously on 890 lots.
